articles.title: Why the search warrants were deemed unlawful and what happens next?
articles.summary: Special correspondent Lucy Manning explains why the Hight Court has ruled that search warrants used to search Mr Mountbatten-Windsor's home were unlawful.
articles.body:
The High Court has heard that search warrants used by Thames Valley Police to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year were unlawful.

The force has said it accepted that the 'initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect', before they searched the former prince's properties on 19 February.

Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested by Thames Valley Police on suspicion of misconduct in public.

He denies any wrongdoing. Special correspondent Lucy Manning is outside the High Court and explains what we know about the ruling.

articles.title: Quem é Nicinha Salviano, nova conselheira de Fernando de Noronha | G1
articles.standfirst: Eleita pela primeira vez, com 156 votos, Nicinha afirma que vai defender os menos favorecidos e priorizar o diálogo.
articles.summary: Eleita pela primeira vez, com 156 votos, Nicinha afirma que vai defender os menos favorecidos e priorizar o diálogo.
articles.body:
Dos sete conselheiros distritais eleitos em Fernando de Noronha no domingo (4), dois não fazem parte da atual composição do Conselho. Artur Cândido já foi conselheiro e retorna ao cargo. Nicinha Salviano foi eleita pela primeira vez, com 156 votos.

O Conselho Distrital exerce funções semelhantes às de uma Câmara de Vereadores. Estreante na Casa, Nicinha afirmou que uma das prioridades do mandato será defender os moradores em menos favorecidos ( veja vídeo acima ).

“Vou trabalhar pelos menos favorecidos e eu me incluo nesse grupo. Quem se criou na ilha, como eu, pegando sal das pedras para cozinhar, dormiu no escuro e teve que plantar para colher o que iria comer, sabe o que eu falo”, afirmou.

Nicinha Salviano é a nova conselheira distrital de Noronha — Foto: Ana Clara Marinho/TV Globo

Eunice José de Souza, conhecida como Nicinha, tem 57 anos, é dona de um restaurante, artesã e faz parte de uma das maiores famílias de Fernando de Noronha. Ela é filha de Salviano José de Souza, pescador tradicional que ajudou a organizar a categoria na ilha.

Seu Salviano teve 28 filhos e dedicou parte da vida à defesa dos pescadores. Em 1956, ele viajou de barco do Recife ao Rio de Janeiro com outros pescadores para participar da posse do presidente Juscelino Kubitschek e pedir apoio aos trabalhadores do mar.

Inspirada no exemplo do pai, Nicinha afirma que pretende usar o diálogo e a negociação como ferramentas de trabalho no Conselho.

“Eu vivo Noronha na prática, não na teoria. Sempre fui de escutar porque eu tive um professor assim, que foi o meu pai. Não sou extremista. Onde mora o extremismo não moram a coerência nem o respeito”, afirmou.

Seu Salviano (de camisa escura) foi de barco para a posse de Juscelino Kubitschek — Foto: Reprodução/Ana Clara Marinho

Nicinha Salviano também afirmou que pretende trabalhar para reduzir as disputas internas no Conselho Distrital.

“A população tem perdido muito com as disputas de ego no Conselho. Quero ser respeitada como ser humano. Enquanto um quer ser mais que o outro, a população cai. As divergências acontecem, mas o respeito precisa existir”, declarou.

A nova conselheira apoiou a reeleição da governadora Raquel Lyra ( PSD ). Segundo Nicinha, o apoio não vai interferir no trabalho de fiscalização das ações da Administração de Fernando de Noronha.

“Eu apoiei a reeleição da governadora, mas a minha prioridade são as minhas pautas em prol de Fernando de Noronha. Isso eu não abro mão. A minha postura de defender a população é inegociável”, afirmou.

Nicinha Salviano também relembrou a atuação da ex-presidente do Conselho Distrital Eunice Oliveira, que tinha a negociação como uma de suas bandeiras.

A nova conselheira afirmou que está preparada para o mandato de quatro anos, que começa em janeiro de 2027.

“Vou trabalhar por uma luta justa para o povo. Quero debater todas as causas e dar uma resposta à confiança de quem votou em mim”, disse Nicinha.

articles.title: Virose em Itapeva: Prefeitura investiga surto com 1,7 mil casos | G1
articles.standfirst: Amostras de água foram coletadas em diferentes pontos da cidade e encaminhadas ao Instituto Adolfo Lutz, em Sorocaba (SP). Em apenas quatro dias, saúde pública atendeu 700 pacientes com os sintomas.
articles.summary: A Prefeitura de Itapeva (SP) enviou amostras da água que abastece a cidade para análise. O objetivo é investigar se há relação entre a qualidade da água e o surto de virose.
articles.body:
A Prefeitura de Itapeva (SP) enviou, nesta quinta-feira (8), amostras da água que abastece a cidade para análise. O objetivo é investigar se há relação entre a qualidade da água e o aumento de casos de virose no município .

Em um mês, cerca de 1,7 mil pacientes procuraram a rede pública de saúde com sintomas da doença. Apenas na Santa Casa do município, foram 300 atendimentos durante todo o mês de setembro, registrando um aumento de quase 200% em comparação ao período anterior.

A apuração da administração municipal começou após 700 pessoas apresentarem sintomas semelhantes em apenas quatro dias. Entre os principais relatos estão vômitos e diarreia.

O aumento da procura também foi percebido em uma farmácia da cidade, que precisou reforçar o estoque de medicamentos usados no tratamento desses sintomas.

Conforme a prefeitura, coletas de água foram feitas em diferentes pontos da cidade e enviadas ao Instituto Adolfo Lutz, em Sorocaba (SP), para uma análise que apontará, em detalhes, se o surto de virose está relacionado à qualidade da água no município.

Santa Casa de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A diretora da Vigilância em Saúde, Juliana Ferreira Carvalho, explica que as equipes também estão buscando identificar se há algum fator em comum entre os pacientes atendidos.

"Estamos fazendo investigação in loco com os pacientes, questionando se as pessoas estiveram em algum evento muito grande na cidade ou fora dela. Todas as informações que conseguirmos tirar por meio das investigações é o que ajudará a chegar a um resultado", detalha.

À TV TEM , a secretária de Saúde de Itapeva, Márcia Moraes, afirma que ainda não há indícios do que provocou o aumento dos casos. Até o momento, ela pontua que não é possível confirmar se o problema é somente na cidade.

"Conhecemos outros casos em outros locais, de pessoas que, inclusive, não vieram a Itapeva. Por isso, temos que tomar muito cuidado e deixar a população tranquila com relação a que, neste momento, não podemos falar que é um problema local. Assim que tivermos uma diagnóstico, explicaremos o que é", esclarece.

Médico reforça a importância da hidratação oral — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Diego Lipe, médico da Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) de Itapeva, destaca que a hidratação é fundamental para um paciente que possui suspeita de gastroenterite.

"Hidratação é fundamental porque, quanto mais diarreia, mais desidratada a pessoa física. Não apenas o soro, mas é importante, também, uma hidratação oral", diz.

Em nota, a Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (Sabesp) informou que fez análises da água nos reservatórios entre os dias 24 e 30 de setembro. Entretanto, nenhuma anomalia foi identificada.

O Centro de Vigilância Epidemiológica do Estado de São Paulo (CVE-SP) informou em nota que aguarda informações complementares da Vigilância Epidemiológica Municipal para definir as medidas necessárias e dar continuidade às investigações.

Em relação às amostras de água, o CVE esclarece que a coleta foi realizada como parte das ações de rotina do Programa ProÁgua. Os resultados das análises poderão contribuir para a investigação epidemiológica e auxiliar na identificação da possível origem do surto.

A TV TEM também entrou em contato com o Instituto Adolfo Lutz para um posicionamento, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação desta reportagem.

Saiba quais são os sintomas de gastroenterite — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A gastroenterite é uma inflamação do estômago e do intestino e pode provocar sintomas como diarreia, vômitos, náuseas, dores abdominais e febre.

Conforme a Secretaria de Saúde de Itapeva, na maioria dos casos, a recuperação pode ocorrer em casa, com alguns cuidados. A principal recomendação é manter a hidratação, consumindo água, soro de reidratação e outros líquidos ao longo do dia para repor a quantidade perdida pelo organismo.

A alimentação também deve ser mantida, dando preferência a alimentos leves e de fácil digestão, como sopas, frutas e torradas. O repouso é indicado enquanto persistirem os sintomas.

Outro cuidado importante é a higiene das mãos, principalmente após ir ao banheiro e antes de preparar ou consumir alimentos. A medida ajuda a reduzir o risco de transmissão da doença para outras pessoas da casa.

A Secretaria de Saúde também orienta que medicamentos sejam utilizados somente com indicação médica.

UPA de Itapeva (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Apesar de muitos casos evoluírem bem com cuidados em casa, alguns sintomas exigem avaliação médica.

A orientação é procurar a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) 24 horas em casos de vômitos persistentes, diarreia intensa ou com presença de sangue, febre alta, dores abdominais fortes ou sinais de desidratação.

Entre os sinais de alerta estão boca seca, pouca produção de urina e fraqueza intensa.

Em casos de sintomas leves ou dúvidas sobre a doença, a recomendação da Secretaria de Saúde é procurar a unidade de saúde mais próxima para avaliação de um profissional.

articles.title: Segurança digital: o que toda empresa deveria saber antes de um ataque | G1
articles.standfirst: Ataques cibernéticos também ameaçam pequenas e médias empresas. Por isso, a segurança digital deve fazer parte da infraestrutura do negócio.
articles.summary: Ataques cibernéticos também ameaçam pequenas e médias empresas. Por isso, a segurança digital deve fazer parte da infraestrutura do negócio.
articles.body:
Ilustração de segurança digital, Imagem: Lorena Valentim - Criada com IA.

Quando o assunto é segurança digital, ainda é comum que pequenas e médias empresas acreditem que não são alvos interessantes para criminosos virtuais. Na prática, o tamanho do negócio não elimina os riscos. Empresas de diferentes setores e portes podem sofrer tentativas de invasão, vazamento de dados, sequestro de arquivos e acessos não autorizados.

E embora ferramentas como antivírus, autenticação em dois fatores e senhas fortes sejam fundamentais, a proteção não começa e termina nos computadores dos colaboradores. A estrutura de rede também precisa fazer parte dessa estratégia.

A segurança digital de uma empresa depende de diferentes camadas de proteção, e uma rede bem estruturada é uma delas. A PGF oferece recursos como IP público fixo, que podem facilitar a configuração de firewalls, VPNs e controles de acesso, enquanto boas práticas de segurança ajudam a reduzir vulnerabilidades e proteger os dados da empresa.

O erro mais comum: tratar segurança como um problema apenas de TI

A segurança digital costuma ser associada exclusivamente à equipe de tecnologia. Mas, na prática, ela envolve toda a infraestrutura utilizada pelo negócio — inclusive a forma como a empresa se conecta à internet.

Uma rede sem controles de acesso adequados, equipamentos mal configurados ou conexões remotas sem proteção podem criar vulnerabilidades que vão além do comportamento dos funcionários.

Por isso, a segurança precisa ser pensada desde a estrutura básica da operação, incluindo a escolha do provedor e dos recursos disponíveis no plano contratado.

IP público fixo: mais controle sobre a rede

Um dos recursos relevantes para determinadas operações empresariais é o IP público fixo. Diferentemente de um IP dinâmico, que pode mudar ao longo do tempo, o IP fixo mantém um endereço público estável para a conexão da empresa.

Essa característica pode facilitar configurações de firewall, VPN, acesso remoto e outras soluções que dependem de um endereço de rede conhecido e estável.

Para empresas que utilizam servidores próprios, sistemas internos, câmeras de segurança ou precisam permitir acessos remotos controlados, esse recurso pode ser especialmente útil.

É importante, porém, entender que ter um IP público fixo não significa estar automaticamente mais protegido. A segurança depende de como esse recurso é configurado e das demais camadas de proteção utilizadas pela empresa.

Por isso, contar com consultores especializados na hora da contratação faz diferença: são eles que ajudam a identificar se a empresa realmente precisa de recursos como IP público fixo ou de um Link Dedicado, e como configurá-los de forma adequada à rotina do negócio — evitando tanto brechas de segurança quanto gastos com recursos que não serão bem aproveitados.

VPN e firewall: camadas importantes de proteção

VPNs, ou redes privadas virtuais, permitem criar uma conexão protegida entre dispositivos e a rede da empresa, sendo especialmente úteis para equipes que trabalham remotamente ou precisam acessar sistemas internos fora do ambiente corporativo.

Já o firewall funciona como uma camada de controle sobre o tráfego da rede, permitindo bloquear ou restringir determinados acessos de acordo com regras definidas pela empresa.

Essas ferramentas não substituem outras práticas de segurança, mas fazem parte de uma estratégia mais ampla de proteção. Quando corretamente configuradas, ajudam a controlar quem pode acessar determinados recursos e quais tipos de conexão são permitidos.

O papel do provedor de internet na infraestrutura de segurança

Um ponto pouco discutido é que a segurança digital também passa pela escolha do provedor de internet. O provedor não é responsável sozinho pela proteção da empresa, mas os recursos oferecidos pela conexão podem facilitar — ou limitar — a implementação de determinadas soluções de rede.

Ter uma conexão estável, IP público fixo e suporte técnico especializado pode fazer diferença para empresas que precisam estruturar VPNs, firewalls, acessos remotos e outras soluções corporativas.

Tempo de resposta também é parte da segurança: quanto mais rápido um problema de conexão é resolvido, menor o tempo em que a empresa fica exposta a instabilidades. Em planos empresariais da PGF Telecom, o suporte segue SLA de até 8 horas, chegando a até 6 horas em planos de Link Dedicado — bem abaixo do prazo de até 48 horas previsto pela Anatel para conexões residenciais.

Além disso, contratar com um provedor regularizado, como a PGF Telecom, significa que toda a estrutura de proteção do lado da conexão — infraestrutura de rede, estabilidade e conformidade com as normas do setor — já está sob responsabilidade do provedor. Isso permite que a empresa direcione sua atenção para a segurança dentro do próprio ambiente de trabalho, sem precisar se preocupar com a parte estrutural da conexão.

A PGF Telecom, provedora de internet 100% fibra óptica com atuação em Caruaru e Recife, oferece IP público fixo em seus planos empresariais, permitindo que seus clientes tenham uma base adequada para implementar diferentes configurações de rede.

Somada à estabilidade da conexão e ao atendimento técnico próximo, essa estrutura contribui para que empresas da região tenham mais autonomia e suporte na construção de uma infraestrutura de conectividade adequada às suas necessidades.

Segurança começa antes do problema aparecer

Investir em segurança digital não deveria ser uma reação a um ataque, mas parte do planejamento de qualquer empresa, independentemente do tamanho ou setor.

Isso significa combinar boas práticas, treinamento das equipes, ferramentas de proteção e uma infraestrutura de rede bem planejada. A escolha do provedor de internet também faz parte dessa equação, especialmente para negócios que dependem de acesso remoto, sistemas internos e transmissão constante de dados.

No ambiente digital, não existe uma única solução capaz de proteger uma empresa de todos os riscos. O caminho mais seguro é construir diferentes camadas de proteção — começar por uma infraestrutura preparada para sustentar as necessidades do negócio.

articles.title: TSE nega registro de candidatura de Garotinho e anula votos; decisão abre caminho para vitória de Ruas no 1º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Maioria dos ministros também votou para rejeitar o pedido de desistência de Garotinho de um recurso contra a decisão que negou sua candidatura.
articles.summary: Maioria dos ministros também votou para rejeitar o pedido de desistência de Garotinho de um recurso contra a decisão que negou sua candidatura.
articles.body:
O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) decidiu nesta quinta-feira (8) negar o registro da candidatura de Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) ao governo do Rio de Janeiro no primeiro turno das eleições do último domingo (4).

Os ministros também decidiram que Garotinho não poderia desistir do recurso que apresentou para tentar liberar sua candidatura (entenda o impasse que levou ao julgamento mais abaixo).

Na discussão sobre o destino dos votos recebidos por Garotinho, a maioria dos ministros decidiu por considerar nulos os votos recebidos por ele.

A decisão abre caminho para a vitória de Douglas Ruas (PL) no primeiro turno.

➡️O julgamento terminou com os seguintes placares:

7 a 0 para negar o registro da candidatura ;

5 a 2 por considerar nulos os votos recebidos .

Com a anulação dos 274.411 votos recebidos por Garotinho, haverá uma retotalização do resultado das urnas.

➡️ Na prática, Ruas deve ser declarado eleito governador do estado no primeiro turno , sem a necessidade de uma nova votação em 25 de outubro. Os 274.411 votos correspondem a 3,17% da votação atribuída a Garotinho.

Votaram pela anulação dos votos o relator Floriano de Azevedo Marques, além dos ministros André Mendonça, Estela Aranha, Dias Toffoli e Kassio Nunes Marques.

Em seu voto, que havia consolidado a maioria pela nulidade dos votos recebidos por Garotinho , o ministro Dias Toffoli afirmou:

"Não é que é nula a capacidade política. Ela é inexistente. O que é inexistente é desconsiderado a qualquer tempo, a qualquer hora. Então, por muito mais razão sendo condições de elegibilidade, não há como computar esses votos como votos válidos para nenhum fim", afirmou.

Os ministros Villas Bôas Cueva e Sebastião Reis Júnior divergiram nesse ponto e votaram para não anular os votos de Garotinho. O placar final sobre a anulação ficou em 5 a 2.

🔎 Na certidão do TSE que proclamou o resultado do julgamento, publicada nesta tarde, a Corte determinou que a situação sub judice — isto é, que ainda dependia de decisão da Corte Eleitoral — da candidatura de Garotinho seja cessada e que o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Rio de Janeiro seja comunicado para as providências cabíveis, que inclui a retotalização dos votos, com a exclusão dos votos atribuídos a Garotinho.

Douglas Ruas e Eduardo Paes — Foto: Leandro Oliveira / TV Globo e Bruno Grubertt / TV Globo

Com a anulação dos votos em Garotinho, a quantidade de votos válidos no pleito são reduzidos, permitindo a Ruas ser declarado governador do Rio sem segundo turno.

No domingo (4), Ruas teve 4.271.199 votos e apareceu com 49,27% dos votos válidos. Paes, segundo colocado, recebeu 3.706.984 votos, ou 42,76%.

Garotinho teve 274.411 votos, equivalentes a 3,17%. Sem os votos de Garotinho na base de cálculo, o percentual dos candidatos subiu. Com isso, Ruas passou a ter 51% dos votos válidos, o que deve fazer dele o governador eleito em primeiro turno.

Em setembro, o TRE considerou Garotinho inelegível, porque ainda estaria sob os efeitos da condenação por improbidade administrativa, dano ao erário e enriquecimento ilícito de terceiros.

O caso chegou ao TSE. Primeiro, a Corte liberou Garotinho para fazer campanha e permitiu acesso a recursos públicos para a campanha. Depois, o caso teve decisões individuais conflitantes.

O relator do caso, Floriano de Azevedo Marques, determinou que os votos de Garotinho deveriam ser anulados. Com isso, não seriam considerados válidos.

Anthony Garotinho participa de coletiva após o debate na Globo — Foto: Globo/Manoella Mello

No domingo, o presidente do TSE, Nunes Marques, fixou que os votos dele seriam considerados no cálculo dos percentuais obtidos pelos candidatos ao governo do Rio até que o plenário da Corte decida sobre a manutenção da rejeição do registro de candidatura.

Depois do resultado nas urnas e diante da indicação de um segundo turno, a defesa de Garotinho acionou o TSE pedindo a desistência do recurso. A medida ajudaria Ruas e provocou críticas, especialmente na campanha de Paes.

O TSE tem entendimento de que a desistência de um recurso é inadmissível quando o ato puder alterar o quociente eleitoral, que define o número de votos necessários.

Isso porque o julgamento do recurso deixa de ser apenas do candidato, porque há um potencial de interferência quanto ao resultado da eleição, passando a ser considerado um interesse de toda a coletividade, ou seja, um direito indisponível.

Nos bastidores, ministros apontam que o caso pode provocar debates no plenário da Corte. A coligação de Eduardo Paes pediu que o TSE deixasse Garotinho fora da disputa, mas reconhecendo os mais de 274 mil votos no cálculo para o quórum, o que manteria o segundo turno.

O Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE), no entanto, entendeu que o caso de Garotinho é uma exceção e que, como ele está inelegível, seria possível acolher a desistência.

articles.title: Latam recebe 1º avião E195-E2 da Embraer, em São José dos Campos | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento foi realizado na manhã desta quinta-feira (8).
articles.summary: Evento foi realizado na manhã desta quinta-feira (8).
articles.body:
Latam recebe 1º avião E195-E2 da Embraer, em São José dos Campos — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

A companhia aérea Latam recebeu, na manhã desta quinta-feira (8), o primeiro avião da Embraer que vai integrar a frota da companhia.

A aeronave, modelo E195-E2, é a primeira de uma série de aviões que devem ser entregues à empresa nos próximos meses. A previsão é que 14 aviões sejam entregues em 5 meses.

O grupo encomendou inicialmente 24 unidades e mantém opções para outras 50, com valor de aproximadamente R$ 2,1 bilhões para a encomenda inicial a preços de tabela.

O modelo E195-E2 terá configuração para 136 passageiros e serão usados inicialmente em rotas domésticas.

Em evento na manhã desta quinta, a Embraer deu detalhes das aeronaves entregues à Latam, especificando que os aviões são de voos de curtas distâncias e pistas curtas, além de 30% de economia em uso de combustível.

articles.title: Bedbugs crawling out the wallpaper in 'worst ever' Cardiff infestation
articles.summary: An infested house in Cardiff was so bad the mattresses and bed frames had to be incinerated.
articles.body:
Millions of bedbugs were crawling out of mattresses in what a pest controller said was the worst outbreak he had seen in 38 years.

They were even in the walls and under the wallpaper, with the mattresses and bed frames needing to be incinerated.

Cardiff pest controller Gareth Davies had to wear full protection as his team tackled the problem in the Canton area of the city, using a specialist vacuum cleaner to collect millions of the bugs.

It came after they had tackled a large cockroach outbreak last month in a scene he likened to a horror movie.

"This house was just horrific," he told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast .

"Hundreds of thousands of them when you lifted the mattresses up.

"They were coming out of the wallpaper, it was horrendous."

Bedbugs can enter homes on clothes, luggage, or second hand furniture - and "hide" in mattresses or walls, according to the NHS .

Bites are the most common sign you have bed bugs - usually raised, itchy, in a line or grouped together.

On white skin the bites usually look red, while on black or brown skin they could be purple and harder to see.

Other things to look out for are spots of blood on bedding - if the bugs have been squashed - or small brown spots on bedding or furniture, which could be their faeces.

"You'll be bitten and you'll see blood spotting on the sheets," Davies said.

"As soon as you see them you need to act."

It can be difficult to get rid if bedbugs but there are steps that can be taken, including:

Washing contaminated bedding and clothing on a hot wash and tumble dry on a hot setting for at least 30 minutes

Putting the clothing or bedding in a plastic bag and put in the freezer for three or four days

Clean the house regularly - bedbugs can be found in both clean and dirty places, but regular cleaning can help to spot them

Davies said at the recent outbreak his team first used specialist vacuum cleaners "to take as many {bed bugs] as we can out of the equation".

"Then we treat with a specialist insecticide, bag all the mattresses and frames and get them incinerated," he added.

Bedbugs most often enter properties attached to luggage, clothing or second-hand furniture.

Once inside they tend to hide close to where people sleep, including in mattresses, bed frames, furniture and small cracks and crevices.

Infestations are not the result of poor hygiene, according to advice from the NHS, which says bedbugs can be found in both clean and dirty homes.

Regular cleaning can help to spot them early, the advice adds.

articles.title: 'Dhappa' gets a Day 3 twist as police allow Rahul, INDIA bloc MPs to protest at Raj Ghat
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Thursday allowed opposition leaders to reach Raj Ghat, where they staged a brief protest against Chief Election Commissioner
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Thursday allowed opposition leaders to reach Raj Ghat, where they staged a brief protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. This came after two days of police stopping INDIA bloc leaders from marching to their chosen protest sites."INDIA alliance MPs staged a peaceful sit-in at Raj Ghat today. Here, they paid homage to Bapu and prayed for the Modi government to be endowed with sound judgment. Modi, Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar are together snatching away the public's right to vote. We will not allow this to happen under any circumstances," Congress said.The change in police approach came on the third day of the opposition's protests over the report of "dissent" in the Election Commission, its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and allegations of "vote chori".On Tuesday, Rahul Gandhi and opposition MPs were stopped as they marched near the Election Commission office. Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi subsequently ducked the cops and staged an eight-hour sit-in at the Akashvani Bhawan complex.The Congress described the surprise move as "dhappa", a Hindi expression for a game of tag or hide-and-seek, and shared a map showing how Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi changed their route to enter the complex after policestopped their march.The opposition met in central Delhi on Wednesday for lunch and, within an hour, attempted to march to Jantar Mantar but was stopped by police, with several leaders, including the Gandhi siblings, being detained. Police also registered FIRs in connection with the two flash protests.On Thursday, the opposition once again came up with a new destination and decided to head to Raj Ghat after a lunch meeting hosted by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge at a restaurant in Connaught Place.The leaders left the venue in buses, with Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other INDIA bloc leaders travelling together.The convoy then reached Raj Ghat, where the leaders held a short protest before leaving.The development was notable because Delhi Police had imposed prohibitory orders at Raj Ghat earlier in the day itself. However, despite the restrictions, the opposition leaders were allowed to reach the memorial.Unlike the previous two days, there was no prolonged face-off between the protesters and police, or mass detention of opposition leaders.The police action and detention of opposition leaders had itself become a major part of the political messaging in the last two days, with Congress leaders accusing the government of preventing them from exercising their right to protest.Ahead of the protest, Rahul Gandhi continued his attack on the government and the Election Commission, alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, home minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and CEC Gyanesh Kumar had "hijacked" India through a "criminal conspiracy". He said they would be "brought to justice".Kharge, meanwhile, said the INDIA bloc leaders would hold a peaceful sit-in at the Gandhi memorial and "pray" for Modi and Shah to be blessed with wisdom.The BJP, meanwhile, hit out at the Congress. Addressing a press conference, spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari questioned Rahul Gandhi, alleging a lack of trust in the Supreme Court to deal with the appeals regarding the SIR exercise. Attacking the Congress, the BJP leader framed it as a fight between the Gandhi-Vadra family and the people of India."The Congress party is fighting against 'We, the People of India.' This battle has become one of the Congress party—its workers and the Gandhi-Vadra family—versus the people of India, who are silently witnessing the party's hooliganism. They used to speak about returning to ballot papers. Yet, we recently saw elections held in places like Assam and Tripura; the Congress party lost there too, even though EVMs were not the only factor," Bhandari said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Ithaca council halts Cornell event permits amid scrutiny over handling of rape allegations
articles.summary: Ithaca Common Council voted 9-1 to block Cornell University permits over the school's handling of Jane Doe's rape allegations against fraternity members.
articles.body: The Ithaca Common Council voted late Wednesday night to stop issuing city permits to Cornell University and affiliated student groups, including fraternities, following widespread criticism of the Ivy League school's handling of rape allegations made by a former student. After hours of debate, the council voted 9-1 in favor of a moratorium, which temporarily bars Cornell from obtaining new permits for assemblies, parades and special events at the Ithaca Commons and activities requiring noise permits, citing public safety concerns. The measure drew support from numerous Cornell students and Ithaca residents, although some graduate students raised concerns that the restrictions were overly broad and could disrupt activities unrelated to Greek life. CORNELL PROTESTERS SWARM CAMPUS TO SUPPORT JANE DOE, CALL FOR UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT'S RESIGNATION One graduate student warned that the moratorium could result in canceled or delayed events, lost deposits, reduced access to venues and disruptions to conferences. The moratorium will stay in place until Nov. 5, unless the council extends it at a later date. The measure also includes an amendment that requires Cornell to refer investigations involving sexual and violent crimes to the Ithaca Police Department, though its unclear how that will be enforced. The moratorium comes after the student, identified as Jane Doe, filed a lawsuit in September accusing seven former Chi Phi fraternity members of drugging and raping her on the night of Oct. 19, 2024, and into the following morning. In the lawsuit, she alleges she arrived at the frat house already intoxicated, after which the men pressured her into taking ketamine and other substances. The men have denied wrongdoing, with some maintaining the sexual activity was consensual and others denying they participated. CORNELL PICKS FORMER DEPUTY US ATTORNEY GENERAL TO REVIEW SEX ASSAULT RESPONSE The fraternity was suspended on Nov. 8, 2024, the same day Doe reported sexual assault allegations to campus police, according to Doe's civil complaint. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten, who initially declined to pursue charges, has said Doe's Nov. 2024 sworn statement did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped and, instead, described her participation in drug use and sexual conduct as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual." However, CBS New York obtained the transcript of the Cornell police interviews with Jane Doe on Nov. 14 and 15, 2024, during which she told investigators: "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." Van Houten said he was never provided the full transcript. Late last month, he announced his office was reopening the case because the allegations contained in Jane Doe's lawsuit differed from her sworn statement nearly two years earlier. BAR NAMED IN CORNELL RAPE LAWSUIT DISPUTES ACCUSER'S ACCOUNT, SAYS SHE WAS NEVER SERVED ALCOHOL WHILE UNDERAGE In an interview with The Associated Press on Wednesday, Jane Doe's lawyer, Thomas Giuffra, said Cornell police led her to believe the criminal investigation remained active even though Van Houten had decided against filing charges just days after she first spoke with investigators. Van Houten has said he instructed Cornell police to inform Jane Doe that charges would not be pursued, but acknowledged he never spoke directly with her or her attorney. Gov. Kathy Hochul effectively took the investigation out of Van Houten's hands on Oct. 1, by appointing Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor on the case. "Newly released information continues to raise serious questions about the investigation conducted by the Cornell Police Department and the decision by the Tompkins County District Attorney not to prosecute an alleged sexual assault on Cornell University's campus in October 2024," Hochul said in a statement. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP She added: "This has, in turn, undercut my faith, and the public's faith, in the District Attorney's ability to effectively investigate and prosecute the case at this time." On Wednesday, one of the men named in Jane Doe's lawsuit petitioned a court to remove James from the case, accusing her of bias over a social media post she made days before her appointment in which she called what Doe allegedly endured "horrific and unacceptable," The Associated Press reported. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Canadian Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articles.summary: The Swedish Academy praised the 76-year-old poet and essayist’s work for being ‘bold and inventive’.
articles.body:
Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature, the award-giving body has announced.

Carson was selected “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the Swedish Academy said in a statement on Thursday.

The 76-year-old, whose work is praised for blurring the lines of poetry and fiction, and for giving ancient works new translation, is also a professor of classics.

She has written more than 20 books, some of which have been adapted into plays, and has received numerous literary awards.

“Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning,” the academy said.

“She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right.”

Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the academy, which ⁠awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2m), said Carson “was very taken by surprise”.

“We didn’t have so much time to speak, and all she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind.”

Shortly after the announcement, Carson reacted to her win to Icelandic broadcaster RUV. “Crazy. I think they’re all crazy … Well, you know, it’s crazy,” she said.

Carson, who was born in Toronto, also spends time in Iceland, where she also has citizenship.

One of her most notable works includes the Beauty of the Husband, a poignant and moving book-length narrative poem depicting a doomed marriage.

The Trojan Women, published in 2021, is a graphic retelling of Euripides’s ancient story, infused with modern vernacular.

In August 2024, she revealed in the London Review of Books that she was living with Parkinson’s disease.

The Nobel Prize, awarded by the Swedish Academy, is widely considered the most prestigious international award in literature.

Last year’s prize was won by Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai .

Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred ‌Nobel, ‌the prizes for achievements in literature, science and peace have been awarded since 1901.

Literature was the fourth of this year’s Nobels to be announced this week, following medicine, physics and chemistry. The peace winner will be announced in Oslo on Friday.

articles.title: Former Prince Andrew wins legal dispute over search warrants after Epstein-linked misconduct arrest
articles.summary: LONDON — Police who searched the properties of the former Prince Andrew and seized his property in the investigation into his links to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have agreed the search warrants were unlawful, a London judge said Thursday.
articles.body: LONDON — Police who searched the properties of the former Prince Andrew and seized his property in the investigation into his links to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have agreed the search warrants were unlawful, a London judge said Thursday. Justice Nicholas Hilliard said that the Thames Valley Police had made a significant error in applying for the warrant when they searched the properties of the former prince now known as Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested on Feb. 19, on suspicion of misconduct in public office and police searched two of his homes. His lawyers asked the High Court judge to invalidate the warrants under which those searches were conducted. Hilliard said the parties had agreed to invalidate the warrants before the hearing Thursday. Mountbatten-Windsor was not in court for the hearing. Stephens, of the Howard Kennedy firm in London, described the hearing as a preliminary skirmish in the broader legal battle. “It’s the first step of Prince Andrew and his lawyers saying, ‘Actually, this is tainted evidence. It was obtained inappropriately,”’ Stephens said. “Therefore it should be excluded from any criminal trial.” King Charles III stripped Mountbatten-Windsor of his princely title last year as he sought to shield the rest of the royal family from the continuing fallout from his younger brother’s links to Epstein. While Mountbatten-Windsor, 66, continues to receive a stipend from the king’s private funds, Buckingham Palace has made it clear that those funds may not be used to fund his effort to challenge the search warrants. The police investigation initially focused on allegations that Mountbatten-Windsor shared sensitive information with Epstein when the former prince was a U.K. trade envoy, but police later said they could also consider other matters. Police questioned Mountbatten-Windsor for 11 hours before releasing him under investigation, meaning he was neither charged nor exonerated. It was the first time in nearly four centuries that a senior British royal was placed under arrest. The allegations against Mountbatten-Windsor came to light when the U.S. Justice Department released millions of pages of documents from its investigation into sex trafficking by Epstein and his connections to a network of wealthy, powerful men around the world. Mountbatten-Windsor’s ties to Epstein have been a source of embarrassment to the royal family for more than a decade. Lawmakers questioned the relationship as far back as 2011, when the then-prince was forced to give up his globetrotting role as the U.K.’s special trade envoy. Eight years later, he failed to explain his continuing ties to Epstein in a disastrous interview with the BBC, ending his career as a working member of the royal family.

articles.title: King David Hotel bombing to consulate row: A timeline of UK-Israel tension
articles.summary: Israel’s order to shut UK’s Jerusalem consulate is the latest downturn in a relationship strained since before 1948.
articles.body:
The British Consulate General in occupied East Jerusalem has ceased operating under that name after Israel ordered it to close in retaliation for the United Kingdom’s sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

However, UK officials insisted on Thursday that it remains open, albeit under its new title of “UK Mission”.

This isn’t the first time tensions have arisen between Israel and the UK, however. Here’s more about the times relations have faltered.

Why did Israel order the British consulate to close?

Last month, Israel gave the UK 30 days to close the consulate , after which it said British diplomats working there would lose their diplomatic status.

The order came a day after Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced the UK would ban imports of all goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank and would bar companies from providing them with services, including financing, construction and real estate.

As the deadline expired, the two governments reached a last-minute compromise, however.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said Israel would allow a team of seven British diplomats to work from the building, while 20 diplomats, including the consul general, would leave Israel. The name of the building has also been changed.

Miliband said the building would not close and would now be called the “UK Mission, Jerusalem”, and insisted that the UK does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close a consulate, which the UK owns and which has stood for nearly 200 years.

Besides assisting UK nationals in Palestine, the mission provides support to Palestinians and generally represents the UK in East Jerusalem, the occupied West Bank and Gaza.

Britain and Israel have mostly enjoyed strong and warm relations. But Israel’s move against the consulate is not the first time there has been tension between them.

Here is a timeline of some of those moments of strain:

Britain’s role in the founding of Israel dates back to a single letter. On November 2, 1917, Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote to Lord Rothschild that the British government viewed the establishment of a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine “with favour”, provided nothing was done to prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities.

Britain went on to rule Palestine under a League of Nations mandate. By the 1940s, Zionist armed groups had turned their guns on the British administration itself.

The deadliest attack came on July 22, 1946. Members of the Irgun, a Zionist underground group, disguised themselves as hotel staff and carried about 350kg of explosives into the basement of the King David Hotel in Jerusalem. The hotel housed the Secretariat of the Government of Palestine and the headquarters of British forces in Palestine and Transjordan.

Menachem Begin, then head of the Irgun, ordered the bombing. The blast killed 91 people: 41 Arabs, 28 Britons, 17 Jews and five others. Begin later became Israel’s prime minister.

The Irgun claimed it had called in three warnings ahead of the explosion by telephone to the hotel switchboard, the French Consulate and the Palestine Post, giving occupants time to evacuate.

The British authorities did not deny that warnings were sent, but maintained that none reached anyone “in an official position with any power to take action”. The exact sequence of events remains contested: some accounts claim the hotel warning was ignored entirely, while others suggest hotel management did not take the threat seriously. What is not disputed is that the building was not evacuated in time.

The Irgun also claimed that a senior British official, Sir John Shaw, refused to act on its warning, which he strenuously denied.

Britain withdrew from Palestine in May 1948, and Israel declared itself an independent state. Amid the war that followed with neighbouring Arab states, British and Israeli forces came close to direct confrontation.

In late December 1948, Israeli forces pushed into Egyptian territory in Sinai. A United States Department of State message to its ambassador in Tel Aviv warned that unless Israeli forces withdrew, Britain would be bound to fulfil its obligations under its 1936 treaty with Egypt, so Israel pulled back.

Days later, however, the two sides clashed in the air. On January 7, 1949, Israeli forces shot down four Royal Air Force Spitfires, and a Hawker Tempest later that day. The precise location is unclear, but some sources place it near the Deir el-Balah area of what is now the Gaza Strip, but was then about 25km (15 miles) inside Egyptian territory. Two British pilots were killed, including the Tempest’s pilot, David Tattersfield. Israel said its pilots had mistaken the British aircraft for Egyptian ones.

On January 8, the UK announced it was sending forces to Aqaba, on modern-day Jordan’s Red Sea coast, at Transjordan’s request. In his diary, David Ben-Gurion wrote that he had consulted his top commanders on how to deal with the threat of British intervention. Washington helped calm things down: President Harry Truman criticised the British handling of the crisis.

Historians still debate how close the two sides came to war. Some argue the UK worked to avoid confrontation and never issued a formal ultimatum. Either way, Britain withheld de jure recognition of Israel until April 1950.

UK weapons embargo over invasion of Lebanon

When Israel invaded Lebanon in June 1982, the UK took action. Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher later wrote that Britain restricted defence sales to Israel in June 1982 in direct response to the invasion. The embargo lasted until 1994.

Foreign Secretary Francis Pym publicly condemned the invasion, and government papers declassified years later show London was furious in private as well. The UK even refused to send Israel gas masks during the 1991 Gulf War, when Iraqi missiles struck Tel Aviv.

The same year – 1982 – the UK went to war with Argentina over the Falkland Islands, and Israel sent arms to the other side.

According to declassified British files, Israel sold Argentina weapons including Skyhawk jets, which killed dozens of British troops. Foreign Secretary Geoffrey Howe personally asked Israel to stop, but his request was ignored. Israeli arms were also routed through Peru so that the UK would not find out.

Israel denied involvement at first but, by 1984, admitted to supplying Argentina in order to sustain its arms industry. British officials suspected another motive, however. They believed Begin, by then prime minister, still bore a grudge against the UK from the Mandate era.

Relations between the UK and Israel have also dipped since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023. More than 74,000 people in Gaza have been killed in Israeli strikes and its siege of the strip, including about 1,400 of those since a supposed US-led “ceasefire” was declared one year ago. Most of the dead are women and children. Thousands more are lost under the rubble and presumed dead.

In September 2024, the UK suspended 30 arms export licences to Israel. In May 2025, it suspended trade talks and sanctioned individuals and companies linked to settler violence. In September 2025, it formally recognised the State of Palestine.

Last September, London went further. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who is himself Jewish, said the UK now regards Israel’s occupation of the West Bank, not just the illegal settlements there, as illegal. He told parliament that Palestinians are being ethnically cleansed by settlers in parts of the West Bank.

Israel’s response was swift. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said he had urged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close the consulate, accusing it of working on behalf of the Palestinian Authority. Israeli Foreign Minister Saar blamed London: “We did not want it to come to this, but the Labour Government’s actions have led us here.”

The compromise has eased the immediate standoff without resolving it. Saar said the UK had agreed not to retaliate, while Miliband said it would hold off on reciprocal action as long as talks remain credible.

“What’s happening here is that Israel and the UK seem to have found some kind of compromise at the 11th hour, at least for now,” Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec said, reporting from London.

“Strictly speaking, the consulate has shut its doors,” she said. “That’s in official language, but practically speaking, there is still a diplomatic presence that is going to be maintained in occupied East Jerusalem by the UK.”

That, she said, “allows both sides to essentially say that they’ve won the argument”.

“We absolutely are at a low point with UK-Israeli relations,” Nedelec said, adding that in a post on X, Saar listed measures including “shuttering that consulate, and he also cited banning some 12 MPs from entering Israel”.

“Gideon Saar also did say, though, that they are allies and that the intelligence sharing continues,” she added.

Israeli anger has been heightened by a resolution passed by the UK’s Green Party at its recent party conference, equating Zionism with “racism” . The party’s leader, Zack Polanski – who is also Jewish – was not present for the vote. However, he liked a post by Green Party member Gill Tavner after the vote, calling on opponents of the motion to “get over yourselves and move on”. “The decision is made. Sometimes they don’t go your way. If you’d prefer to be with genocidal Labour, maybe just go,” she wrote.

Nihad Abu Ghosh, a Palestinian journalist, told Al Jazeera from Ramallah that Israel’s reaction to rising opposition in the UK to its war on Gaza is “driven by the election context, and by its heightened stance towards those it sees as infringing on or undermining Israel’s sovereignty”.

“Britain recognises the Palestinian state, and Israel is trying to resist that by all possible means,” he said, noting that Israel has also punished Spain, Norway and Ireland over the issue.

He compared the move with Washington’s decision to close its own Jerusalem consulate and handle Palestinian affairs through its embassy. “This is what Israel wants: it wants every country in the world to deal with Palestinians as an Israeli matter,” he said.

“Israel’s problem here is that it is punishing itself,” Abu Ghosh said. “If this involved only one country and a limited, partial tension with a country here or there, it could indeed take tough measures. But this is a widening trend.”

He also linked the standoff to history. “Britain in particular bears primary historical responsibility for the creation of the State of Israel, for supporting it, for suppressing the Palestinian people,” he said, citing the Balfour Declaration. “Unless Israel reverses its policies, the situation is likely to escalate further.”

articles.title: Carlsberg plans to shut Marston's Brewery in Burton
articles.summary: Burton-upon-Trent's links with beer and brewing date back centuries.
articles.body:
Marston's Brewery could close in Burton-upon-Trent, under plans revealed by its owners.

Carlsberg Britvic said it was proposing to shut the facility together with its primary logistics operation based at that site next summer. About 310 people are affected.

Burton-upon-Trent's connections with the brewing industry date back centuries, with the firm describing its own history and legacy in the town as "iconic".

However, it said the "stark reality" was that UK cask ale volumes had more than halved in less than a decade and "this trend looks set to continue across the UK".

The company said "priority brands" including Hobgoblin, McEwan's and Brooklyn were expected to remain in its portfolio, but it is unclear where they will be brewed.

Other, smaller brands could find a home under specialist or local brewers, the firm said.

Some have described Burton as the "beer capital of England", and at its height more than 30 breweries once operated from there.

The Staffordshire town's connection with beer dates back to the 11th Century when monks first started brewing, and Marston's own links to Burton date back more than 200 years.

Camra chairman Ash Corbett-Collins, who grew up in Burton, said statements from Carlsberg about understanding the importance of the brewery to the town "come far too little too late for most people".

"This announcement is an absolute disgrace, and the latest in a string of actions that show how little they care about our brewing heritage or the nation's drinkers."

But he agreed "with Carlsberg on one thing", adding the "time is right to think about alternative, independent, brewers who are willing to become custodians of Carlsberg's cask brands".

Carlsberg Britvic said it told colleagues and trade union partners the news earlier on Thursday.

CEO Paul Davies said the proposal was "by no means a reflection on any of our people, and every effort will be made to help them through this period of uncertainty".

He added Marston's Brewery and the primary logistics operation were expected to continue to operate "during the transition period, while the company works through the detail of the consultation".

"As and when key decisions are taken over the coming months, we will share further information with the industry, but always with our colleagues first."

Davies said it was important to ensure the firm's portfolio was focused "where consumers are today, and where customer demand is growing".

He added: "That said, smaller ale brands are much loved by select consumers, and we will do everything we can to ensure they thrive under more specialist or local ownership in the future."

It is not the first big brewing firm to move operations in the West Midlands.

Banks's Brewery in Wolverhampton ended operations in 2025, with production moving to Burton.

The brewery opened in 1875, but in 2024 Carlsberg Marston's Brewing Company (CMBC) announced it would close as part of a company restructuring.

That year, Carlsberg acquired Marston's PLC's remaining 40% shareholding in CMBC, giving Carlsberg full ownership of the brewing business, including Marston's Brewery and its portfolio of beer brands.

Hospitality firm Marston's PLC is now a completely separate operation. It runs more than 1,300 pubs across the UK from its base in Wolverhampton and is unaffected by Thursday's news.

Burton beer is known for its earthy, eggy smell - known in brewing circles as "Burton snatch" - a sure sign of the ale's quality and provenance.

This is created by the water trickling through unusually thick bands of gypsum under the town, before resting in underground aquifers.

Staffordshire County Council's leader, Reform's Martin Murray, said British beer was famous across the world and over the years much of that had come out of Burton.

"For us to lose that heritage personally saddened me greatly," he said.

The leader of the opposition at the authority, Conservative Philip White, said the "decision means Marston's Pedigree and Bass Ale will no longer be brewed in Burton".

He added: "We must do everything we can to try and reverse this decision and look after all of the workers and their families."

articles.title: Italy’s Giorgia Meloni forces through new electoral law ahead of vote, opposition cries foul
articles.summary: ROME — Italy’s lower house of parliament gave final approval on Thursday to a fiercely contested electoral reform championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni which ⁠provides the framework for a national election due next year.
articles.body: ROME — Italy’s lower house of parliament gave final approval on Thursday to a fiercely contested electoral reform championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni which ⁠provides the framework for a national election due next year. Meloni says the new rules are intended to increase the prospect of stable government. The centre-left opposition says the goal is to boost her chances of retaining power. In a secret ballot, lawmakers approved by 227 votes to 164 a bill introducing a fully proportional electoral system (PR), with a seat bonus guaranteeing a parliamentary majority to any alliance ⁠winning more than 42% of the vote. Under the previous rules, ​around ⁠two-thirds of lawmakers were elected through PR, with the remainder chosen in first-past-the-post constituencies which analysts said may have favoured the opposition. Rules ‘designed to promote stability’ “We are introducing rules designed to promote ⁠the stability and parliamentary cohesion of any government,” Meloni posted on X after the vote. “Whoever wins must be able ​to govern.” When ⁠the reform was conceived, her rightist bloc ‌led in opinion polls and critics said the changes were intended to hand her a handsome majority after the election. However, the political landscape has changed since the emergence in February of a new far-right party, National Future, which ‌has eroded support for the ruling parties. Polls now show the coalition ‌trailing the centre-left and some analysts say the electoral reform may backfire on Meloni, whose government last month celebrated almost four years in power, making it Italy’s longest-lasting since World War Two. In a heated debate, centre-left lawmakers accused the government of flouting democracy by forcing through the new rules ahead ⁠of an election, against the will of the opposition. “Go ahead and change the electoral law, we will win in any case under any voting system,” said Democratic Party (PD) leader Elly Schlein. One element in the reform obliges each coalition or party running outside a coalition to name its candidate for prime minister before the election. This puts the centre-left in a bind because the leaders of its two main parties, the PD and the 5-Star Movement, led by former Prime Minister Giuseppe Conte, are at loggerheads over who should become prime minister if the alliance wins. Coalition tensions Final approval ‌of the reform required four parliamentary votes and capped months of coalition infighting that cast doubt on ​Meloni’s grip on her alliance ahead of next year’s election. The tensions centred on an element ‌of the reform allowing voters to choose their preferred ⁠candidates among party lists, reducing the power of the leaders to control which ones are elected. A compromise was ⁠eventually found by which candidates at the top of the lists are automatically given preference, leaving intact the power of the party chiefs to determine ‌most of the candidates who get ​into parliament. “To those who hoped to see the centre-right ‌divided, today we responded with facts: we are united, ​cohesive, and determined to carry forward the commitments made to citizens,” Meloni said.

articles.title: Lurgan: Maintenance man found woman dead in bath, inquest hears
articles.summary: Laura Marshall's body was discovered in an overflowing bath at her home in April 2016.
articles.body:
The body of a 31-year-old Lurgan woman was found in a bath by a maintenance man who was investigating a leak in the block of flats she had been living in, an inquest has heard.

Laura Marshall's bruised body was discovered in an overflowing bath at her home in Victoria Street in April 2016.

According to a police officer, who was one of the first on the scene, he believed a violent assault had taken place.

A man was arrested and charged with her murder. He denied any involvement in her death. Two years later the case against him was dropped after the Public Prosecution Service (PPS) decided to withdraw all charges.

During the first day of the inquest, a statement from the maintenance man was read out to the court.

He told how another resident in the block of flats had complained that there was water pouring through his ceiling.

He said he had gone to the flat above where Laura Marshall had lived. He said the resident from the flat below had then gone with him to her flat.

The man told the court that the lock on the front door of her flat was loose and that he had been able to force it open.

He said he called out Marshall's name but that there was no answer.

The flat, he said, was in darkness and that he had entered using a torch.

He noted that the floor mat in the hall was sodden and that the door handle of the bathroom was on the floor in the hall. The spindle was not in the lock.

Unable to open the door, the maintenance man had gone downstairs to his van to get a screwdriver which enabled him to unlock the door which had a childproof button on it.

He said he opened the door a few inches and with the aid of his torch he saw Laura Marshall in the bath face down. She was naked and he noticed bruising on her shoulder. The taps were still running.

The sink had been smashed and lay in pieces on the floor and there was blood on the floor.

He said he reported it immediately to the police and that during the call he asked the police if he could turn off the running taps to which he was told he could.

During an opening statement, a lawyer for the coroner said that Laura Marshall had been living with Gary O'Dowd at the property for a few years and that there had been a number of complaints of domestic violence against him.

A detective sergeant, who was among the first members of the PSNI on the scene, also gave evidence.

He too described the bathroom scene. He noted that there was a circular bruise on Laura's forehead and also bruising on her arm.

He said he saw congealed blood higher than the water level of the bath.

In his evidence he said he assessed that the death was suspicious and that it had the "hallmarks of a domestic violence-related murder."

He said in his initial assessment of the scene, he believed that Marshall had taken refuge in the bathroom and that a violent assault had taken place there. Adding that the assault had ended with the victim drowned in the bath.

He also noted that the sink had been smashed and that the inside door handle and spindle were on the floor of the bathroom.

A forensic scientist also gave evidence to the court. During questioning by a lawyer acting on behalf of Laura Marshall's family he said that both the door frame and the bathroom door had been damaged when he examined the scene.

He was asked if it was possible to lock the bathroom door from the outside. He replied: 'Yes".

The inquest is expected to last until at least the end of next week.

articles.title: What were Trump operatives doing for pro-Russian politician Dodik in Bosnia?
articles.summary: Reports that Trump aides were paid to advise Bosnian Serb leader ahead of parliamentary election raise alarm.
articles.body:
A New York Times report has raised questions about what two key political operatives for US President Donald Trump were doing visiting pro-Russian politician Milorad Dodik in Bosnia and Herzegovina ahead of parliamentary elections there on Sunday.

According to sources cited by the US newspaper, James Blair and Chris LaCivita advised Dodik and were paid hundreds of thousands of dollars for their work.

The revelation has triggered a wave of criticism from within the Republican Party. Blair currently runs Trump’s main fundraising organisation, MAGA Inc, while LaCivita is a senior adviser to Trump.

Blair, who has previously served as Trump’s deputy chief of staff, and LaCivita have not commented on the visit.

The Bosnian Serb is a pro-Russian politician in Bosnia and Herzegovina. He last met Russian President Vladimir Putin on September 29 in Moscow in a notably cordial meeting, just five days before Bosnia and Herzegovina’s general election.

Last November, the Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina – the country’s highest – upheld a ban on Dodik from formally running in this year’s October 4 elections, after a Sarajevo court convicted him of refusing to comply with decisions issued by the international envoy overseeing the country’s peace deal.

The former president of Bosnia’s autonomous Serb Republic – or Republika Srpska – was sentenced in February to one year in prison for defying Christian Schmidt, the German diplomat responsible for safeguarding the 1995 peace accords that ended Bosnia’s war in the 1990s.

He was also banned from holding political office for six years and stripped of his post as president.

Dodik nevertheless campaigned for the election. His pro-Russian, nationalist SNSD party went on to celebrate major wins on multiple levels. It won more than 55 percent of votes in regional elections, maintaining its strong grip on power in the Serb-dominated entity of Republika Srpska.

Dodik has led Republika Srpska since 1998, with brief interruptions. He advocates the secession of the entity, established in 1995 under the Dayton Peace Agreement and its eventual unification with neighbouring Serbia – a position that has raised fears of a new conflict in the country and the wider region.

Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina was achieved in 1995 after four years of bloody conflict and genocide against Bosniak Muslims, under pressure from the administration of US President Bill Clinton, at a US military base in Dayton, Ohio. The agreement therefore became known as the Dayton Peace Agreement.

Ironically, Dodik then came to power with the backing of the US administration, as an alternative to the Serbian nationalists who dominated the political scene at the time. Madeleine Albright, then US secretary of state, famously described him as a “breath of fresh air” in the Balkans.

Dodik soon turned against US interests, however, and moved closer to Russia. After Donald Trump returned to power in 2025, he again sought to establish closer relations with Washington. During the 2024 US election campaign, he was seen wearing a MAGA hat.

He appears to have achieved at least some of his goals. Although he had been under US sanctions for years over his role in destabilising Bosnia and Herzegovina, those sanctions were lifted this year. The Trump administration said the move was pragmatic and aimed at easing tensions in the country. In return, Dodik dropped several unconstitutional laws.

How did key Trump advisers end up working for Dodik?

The New York Times reported that James Blair and Chris LaCivita were hired through a Washington law firm retained by the government of Republika Srpska.

According to sources cited by the newspaper, each received hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Documents filed with the US Department of Justice show that Republika Srpska has paid more than $4m since the beginning of 2025 to lobbyists and political operatives linked to Trump for lobbying activities.

The issue of Republika Srpska using public funds to pay lobbying firms recently also reached the Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina. On September 25, the court ruled that Republika Srpska’s lobbying acts and activities were not in accordance with the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina as their objectives were contrary to the constitution, decisions of the Constitutional Court or the institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Ivana Korajlic of Transparency International told Al Jazeera that Republika Srpska would likely not stop lobbying, “it will only be presented in a different way”.

LaCivita previously worked as a political campaign strategist for Sali Berisha, one of the most influential Albanian politicians of the post-socialist period, in the run up to Albanian elections last year.

Berisha is a former president of Albania (1992-1997) and prime minister (2005–2013), and is currently the leader of Albania’s opposition, centre-right Democratic Party.

The administration of former US President Joe Biden banned Berisha from entering the United States in 2021, citing corruption and the misuse of public funds as the reasons. Berisha denied the allegations.

In June this year , during Trump’s second term as US president, it was reported that the US had lifted the travel ban on him and members of his family, just as it had done with Dodik.

How have Republicans reacted to Trump advisers visiting Republika Srpska?

The news prompted reactions within the Republican Party, particularly because of the timing.

Blair and LaCivita were in Republika Srpska at a time when Trump’s political operation was focused on the final stretch of its campaign for midterm congressional elections in the US. According to polls, Republicans are not performing well among voters amid the war on Iran, which has proved deeply unpopular in the US.

Steve Bannon, Trump’s former chief strategist, called Blair and LaCivita “grifters” and demanded a detailed review of the money they had received, Politico reported.

Trump initially said he was unaware of Blair and LaCivita’s other engagements and that he would ask them who else they were working for. He added that if he found a conflict of interest, he would fire them immediately.

Later, responding to questions from reporters in the Oval Office, Trump softened his rhetoric.

Trump said Blair and LaCivita did not actually have a conflict of interest because they were not currently White House employees and, as consultants, are allowed to have multiple clients.

Why would Dodik hire Trump’s political operatives?

It is unclear what Dodik gains by hiring people close to Trump.

Aleksandar Trifunovic, editor of Buka magazine in Banja Luka, said he could see no concrete result from their work advising Dodik.

“We don’t see anything that would allow us to say: ‘This is what they taught him, and that is why he won the election.’ Dodik’s rhetoric has not changed. It has been similar to MAGA rhetoric for a long time. But it was important for Dodik to be able to say that he had Trump’s people working for him. So what Dodik paid for and what he got was proximity to Trump through Trump’s people,” Trifunovic told Al Jazeera.

Trifunović said he views the answer to why Trump’s political operatives would work for Dodik through the lens of the pragmatic nature of the US political system. The American lobbying system is relatively transparent.

“The more money you give, the more support you get,” he said.

However, Trifunovic singled out the relationship between Trump’s political circle and Dodik as particularly significant, given Dodik’s ties to Russia and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

“The main criticism is actually something else: how is it possible that Trump’s people are on good terms with someone who has such close relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin? You cannot be with both Trump and Putin at the same time. That certainly does not have a great future,” Trifunovic said.

What effect could this have on Trump-Dodik relations?

Dodik’s ties to Trump’s political circle have a broader context.

Miljan Kovac, an editor and political commentator from Nevesinje in southeastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, said Trump and the Republicans have given Dodik political space after years of US sanctions imposed on him, members of his family and his associates.

The lifting of sanctions against Dodik last October was justified by the US administration as a pragmatic move aimed at easing tensions in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

“Dodik was clearly bargaining with the US administration, in his own way,” Kovac told Al Jazeera.

On election night, after declaring victory for his SNSD party, Dodik himself spoke about the significance of Trump’s return to the political stage in the United States.

“If it had not been for Trump’s magnificent victory, we would probably be political corpses today. But thanks to the new environment, we are now political winners,” Dodik said.

articles.title: London voters go to polls for Holborn and St Pancras by-election
articles.summary: The vote in London’s Holborn and St Pancras parliamentary seat tests whether Burnham can restore faith in Labour.
articles.body:
Londoners are voting in a special by-election in the electoral district of Holborn and St Pancras, where the Green Party is posing a threat to Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s Labour Party.

Zack Polanski, leader of Britain’s left-wing Greens, was among candidates bidding on Thursday to win the parliamentary seat vacated by the resignation of former Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

Labour has held the seat continuously since its creation in 1983. Thursday’s vote is widely considered a two-horse race with the Greens, with thousands of activists from both parties out canvassing in recent weeks.

The vote is seen as a first test of whether Burnham can restore voters’ faith in Labour, which saw its popularity among left-wing voters plunge over the war in ⁠⁠⁠⁠Gaza .

The by-election also offers him a chance to rob the Greens of the momentum they have built up under Polanski , the 43-year-old self-styled “eco-populist” who became party leader in September last year.

Green gains in areas of London contributed to Labour’s dismal local election results in May, which helped ⁠⁠⁠⁠set in train a process that culminated on July 20 with Starmer’s resignation and his replacement by Burnham.

He has since adopted a tougher position on Israel and seeks to blunt the Greens’ rise by laying out a more left-wing vision for the UK.

Polanski, as the Greens’ candidate, faces Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali, a local council leader who arrived in Britain as a child refugee from Somalia in the 1990s and is expected to be declared the winner.

Polls are scheduled to close at 10pm local time (21:00 GMT) and the result is expected to be announced in the early hours of Friday.

The other candidates are: Barmy Brunch of the Official Monster Raving Loony Party; Ewan Cameron, Conservative Party; independent candidate Tom Darwood; Clare Fischer of the Climate Party; George Galloway, Workers Party; Tyler Johnson, Restore Britain; Briony Anne Lonbay Kapoor of Rejoin EU; Peter Newman of Reform UK; Ketankumar Pipaliya, UK VOICE; Jonathan Silberman of the Communist League; Helen Spiby-Vann, Christian Peoples Alliance; Patrick Thomas Stillman, Liberal Democrats; Ben Walker, UKIP.

articles.title: UK ex-prince Andrew search warrants quashed after police accept legal error
articles.summary: London-based judge says error ‘does not bring investigation to an end’ as police probe disgraced former royal.
articles.body:
Police in the United Kingdom have agreed that warrants they secured to search properties linked to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor ⁠had been issued unlawfully and must be quashed, but they say the investigation into King Charles’s younger brother is ongoing.

High Court Justice Nicholas Hilliard said on Thursday that the Thames Valley Police had made a “significant error” in applying for the warrant when they searched the properties of the former British prince, and that police had agreed that “the search warrants were unlawful”.

But he added, “The fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring an investigation to an end, or mean that the whole of the investigation was unlawful.”

Thames Valley Police said it agreed the warrants were not properly granted by the courts.

“We accept the position that the initial court’s decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore, these must be legally quashed,” a Thames Valley Police spokesperson said.

“Legal proceedings are currently ongoing to decide how material seized during the searches will be managed and whether we can lawfully retain it in support of our ongoing investigation,” he added.

King Charles III’s brother was arrested on his 66th birthday in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office related to his links to late American sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

While he was released later that day, he remains under investigation.

Mountbatten-Windsor was also stripped of his royal titles last year following his connections to Epstein, who died in a New York prison in the United States in August 2019.

The disgraced royal has denied wrongdoing.

Police searched his former home in Windsor, west of London, and Sandringham, eastern England, but he subsequently launched a legal challenge over the legality of the warrants obtained.

At a hearing at London’s High Court on Thursday, Judge Hilliard said the police force was applying to ⁠keep the seized property, which Mountbatten-Windsor was opposing, and the issue would not be settled until ⁠next year.

The spokesperson for Thames Valley Police said it had not returned any material to the royal other than that which was not deemed to be connected to their investigation.

articles.title: Veteran actor Nana Patekar dies of cardiac arrest: Why every minute counts
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The death of veteran actor Nana Patekar at 75 has put the spotlight on sudden cardiac arrest, a medical emergency in which the heart abruptly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The death of veteran actor Nana Patekar at 75 has put the spotlight on sudden cardiac arrest, a medical emergency in which the heart abruptly stops pumping blood effectively and requires immediate resuscitation.According to details shared about his final hours, Patekar reportedly felt unwell in the early hours and was later found sweating and losing consciousness at his residence in Dona Paula, Goa. He was taken to Manipal Hospital, where doctors attempted to revive him with CPR for around 45 minutes to an hour but could not save him, said Dr Shekhar Salkar.Dr Ambuj Roy, Professor of Cardiology at AIIMS Delhi, said cardiac arrest can ultimately be the final common pathway of several serious medical emergencies. “If somebody is feeling unwell, particularly at night, you should immediately call for help and take the person to a hospital,” he said.Once cardiac arrest occurs, the priority is immediate CPR and defibrillation. “Once cardiac arrest occurs, CPR should be started immediately, within two minutes of the onset of cardiac arrest, and a defibrillator used as soon as possible,” he said.The urgency of starting CPR quickly is underscored by its steep impact on survival. Dr Rakesh Garg, professor at AIIMS and an expert involved in developing Indian CPR guidelines, said the chances of survival can decrease by 7% to 10% with every minute without intervention.“If possible, a layperson should start CPR as soon as possible,” Garg said. Chest compressions act as a manual pump, helping circulate blood to the brain and other vital organs until professional medical help arrives. The circulation generated by CPR is not the same as that produced by a normally functioning heart, but it can help keep vital organs supplied with blood while emergency treatment is arranged.For a sudden collapse in an adult, a bystander can start hands-only CPR with chest compressions rather than wait for formal training or mouth-to-mouth rescue breathing, provided the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally.Garg said prolonged interruption of blood flow can deprive the brain of oxygen and cause brain injury. Medical intervention after eight to 10 minutes without effective resuscitation may be too late, he said, adding that brain injury can occur within 10 to 15 minutes.He urged families to learn basic CPR so they can begin chest compressions while waiting for an ambulance or medical team, particularly when someone suddenly becomes unresponsive at home.Garg also said unexplained symptoms should not be ignored, particularly by people with cardiac risk factors. For those living alone, recognising warning symptoms early and seeking medical attention promptly becomes even more important, he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
